results.Keywords: trend, time-series, line, growth, timeline, progress, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
results.When to Use: Data has a time axis; user needs to observe rise/fall trends or rate of change over a continuous period
results.When NOT to Use: Fewer than 4 data points (use stat card); more than 6 series (visual noise); no time dimension exists
results.Data Volume Threshold: <1000 pts: SVG; ≥1000 pts: Canvas + downsampling; >10000: aggregate to intervals
results.Color Guidance: Primary: #0080FF. Multiple series: distinct colors + distinct line styles. Fill: 20% opacity
results.Accessibility Notes: Use solid, dashed, and dotted line styles plus direct series labels; never distinguish series by hue alone.
results.A11y Fallback: Visible data table plus concise trend summary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores the full range.

results.Keywords: waffle, percentage, proportion, progress, filled, grid, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
results.When to Use: Showing what fraction of a whole is filled; percentage progress in a visually engaging and accessible format
results.When NOT to Use: More than 5 categories (use stacked bar); exact values matter over visual proportion; very tight space
results.Data Volume Threshold: 10×10 grid standard (100 cells); for > 5 categories switch to stacked 100% bar
results.Color Guidance: 3–5 categories max. 2–3px gap between cells. Each category a distinct accessible color pair
results.Accessibility Notes: Label each category and percentage and add patterns or symbols; filled-cell color alone is insufficient.
results.A11y Fallback: Percentage table/list plus part-to-whole summary. Keyboard: focus reveals each cell value.

results.Keywords: anomaly, outlier, spike, alert, detection, monitoring, deviation, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
results.When to Use: Monitoring a time-series for outliers; alerting users to unexpected spikes or dips in operational data
results.When NOT to Use: Anomalies are predefined categories (use bar with highlight); real-time context without a pause control
results.Data Volume Threshold: Stream at ≤60fps with Canvas; batch: up to 10,000 pts; mark anomalies as a separate data layer
results.Color Guidance: Normal: #0080FF solid line. Anomaly marker: #FF0000 circle + filled. Alert band: #FFF3CD background zone
results.Accessibility Notes: Mark anomalies with a distinct shape and text annotation as well as color. Do not rely on color alone.
results.A11y Fallback: Anomaly event list/table plus narrative alert summary. Keyboard: focus reveals point details; alerts are available in the persistent list without hover.

results.Keywords: waterfall, cumulative, variance, incremental, bridge, delta, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
results.When to Use: Showing how individual positive/negative components add up to a final total (e.g., P&L, budget variance)
results.When NOT to Use: Changes are not additive; more than 12 bars (readability breaks); audience expects a simple total
results.Data Volume Threshold: 4–12 bars optimal; beyond 12 aggregate minor items into a single 'Other' bar
results.Color Guidance: Increases: #4CAF50. Decreases: #F44336. Start total: #2196F3. End total: #0D47A1. Running total line: dashed
results.Accessibility Notes: Pair increase/decrease bars with signed values and directional icons, not red/green alone. Do not rely on color alone.
results.A11y Fallback: Running-total table plus variance summary. Keyboard: focus reveals the same value as hover.

results.Keywords: process, mining, variants, path, bottleneck, log, event, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
results.When to Use: Analyzing event logs to visualize actual process flows; identifying bottlenecks and deviations in ops/product funnels
results.When NOT to Use: No event log data available; audience expects a static flowchart (use diagram tool); node count > 100 without pre-filtering
results.Data Volume Threshold: <30 nodes: SVG; 30–100: Canvas; >100: apply variant filtering (top 80% of cases) before rendering
results.Color Guidance: Happy path: #10B981 thick line. Deviations: #F59E0B thin line. Bottleneck nodes: #EF4444 fill
results.Accessibility Notes: Label nodes and paths and use shapes/line styles in addition to color; bottlenecks require text annotations. Do not rely on color alone.
results.A11y Fallback: Path summary table plus bottleneck narrative. Keyboard: Move buttons replace drag; focus reveals node details; Enter activates a node; Back returns.

results.Keywords: flow, process, sankey, distribution, source, target, transfer, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
results.When to Use: Showing how quantities flow between nodes; multi-source multi-target distribution
results.When NOT to Use: Flow directions form loops (use network graph); fewer than 3 source-target pairs; mobile-primary context
results.Data Volume Threshold: <50 flows: SVG; ≥50: Canvas; >200 flows: aggregate minor flows into 'Other' node
results.Color Guidance: Gradient from source to target color. Flow opacity: 0.4–0.6. Node labels always visible
results.Accessibility Notes: Label source, target, and value; use line style or node symbols in addition to gradient color. Do not rely on color alone.
results.A11y Fallback: Source-to-target flow table plus flow summary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; Enter/Space drills into a node; Back returns.

results.Keywords: funnel, flow, conversion, drop-off, pipeline, stages, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
results.When to Use: Sequential multi-stage process; showing conversion or drop-off rates between defined stages
results.When NOT to Use: Stages aren't sequential; values don't decrease monotonically (use bar); fewer than 3 stages
results.Data Volume Threshold: 3–8 stages optimal; beyond 8 stages group minor steps into 'Other'
results.Color Guidance: Stages: single color gradient (start → end). Show conversion % between each stage. Highlight biggest drop
results.Accessibility Notes: Keep stage names and values visible and distinguish stages with text and boundaries, not only a gradient. Do not rely on color alone.
results.A11y Fallback: Linear stage table/list plus conversion summary. Keyboard: focus reveals stage values; Enter/Space drills in; Back returns.

results.Keywords: 3d, spatial, immersive, terrain, molecular, volumetric, point-cloud, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
results.When to Use: Scientific/engineering context where Z-axis carries essential info not expressible in 2D
results.When NOT to Use: 2D projection conveys the same insight; mobile context; accessibility-required environments; standard business dashboards
results.Data Volume Threshold: WebGL required. Deck.gl: up to 1M points. Three.js: LOD required beyond 50,000 pts
results.Color Guidance: Depth cues: lighting and shading. Z-axis: color gradient (cool → warm). Transparent overlapping: opacity 0.4
results.Accessibility Notes: Use labels, shapes, and depth-independent cues; color and 3D position cannot be the only carriers of meaning.
results.A11y Fallback: Mandatory 2D projection, data table, and spatial summary. Keyboard: rotate/pan buttons and +/- zoom controls replace pointer/VR manipulation; Reset returns the camera.

results.Keywords: stock, trading, ohlc, candlestick, finance, price, volume, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
results.When to Use: Financial time-series with Open/High/Low/Close data; trading or investment product context only
results.When NOT to Use: Non-financial audience; no OHLC data available (use line chart); accessibility-first context
results.Data Volume Threshold: Real-time: Canvas required. Historical: paginate by time range. Max 500 candles visible at once
results.Color Guidance: Bullish: #26A69A. Bearish: #EF5350. Volume bars: 40% opacity below. Body fill vs hollow for OHLC style
results.Accessibility Notes: Use filled versus hollow candles and OHLC text values; bullish/bearish meaning cannot depend on color. Do not rely on color alone.
results.A11y Fallback: Sortable OHLC table plus daily-change summary. Keyboard: focus reveals candle values; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores range; live updates do not steal focus.

results.Keywords: part-to-whole, pie, donut, percentage, proportion, share, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
results.When to Use: ≤5 categories; one dominant segment vs rest; emphasis on visual proportion over exact values
results.When NOT to Use: Categories > 5; slice differences < 5% (visually indistinguishable); user needs precise values; accessibility-first context
results.Data Volume Threshold: Max 6 slices; beyond that switch to stacked bar 100%
results.Color Guidance: 5–6 max colors. Contrasting palette. Largest slice at 12 o'clock. Always label slices with %
results.Accessibility Notes: Pie charts do not inherently fail WCAG; unlabeled color-only slices are inaccessible. Use direct labels and patterns, with a non-pie fallback. Do not rely on color alone.
results.A11y Fallback: Percentage data table and concise part-to-whole summary; offer a stacked bar view. Keyboard: focus reveals slice values; Enter/Space drills in; Back button returns.

results.Keywords: geographic, map, location, region, geo, spatial, choropleth, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
results.When to Use: Data has a regional/location dimension; spatial distribution is the core insight for the user
results.When NOT to Use: Regions have very different sizes making visual comparison misleading (use bar); mobile-primary context

results.Do: Keep displacement under 2px so it reads as feedback not motion
results.Don't: Don't animate layout-affecting props (width/height/margin) on hover
results.Performance Notes: Runs on transform/opacity only so it stays on the compositor thread

results.GSAP Snippet: gsap.to(el, { y: -4, scale: 1.02, boxShadow: '0 12px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.12)', duration: 0.25, ease: 'power2.out' });
results.Framework Notes: Use gsap.quickTo(el, 'y') for cards with many hover targets to avoid re-creating tweens every event; Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
results.Do: Pair with a matching mouseleave tween that reverses the same properties
results.Don't: Don't leave the hover state stuck if the pointer leaves fast; always attach the reverse tween
results.Performance Notes: quickTo() avoids GC churn on lists with 20+ hoverable cards

results.GSAP Snippet: const onPointerMove = (e) => { const r = el.getBoundingClientRect(); xTo((e.clientX - r.left - r.width / 2) * 0.3); yTo((e.clientY - r.top - r.height / 2) * 0.3); }; el.addEventListener('pointermove', onPointerMove); return () => el.removeEventListener('pointermove', onPointerMove);
results.Framework Notes: Keep a stable named pointer handler so cleanup removes the same function; in React/Vue return the removeEventListener cleanup; use gsap.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') and render x/y at the final neutral state
results.Do: Clamp the pull strength (e.g. * 0.3) so the element never fully leaves its hit box
results.Don't: Don't apply magnetic effect to more than 1-2 focal elements per screen; it becomes noisy
results.Performance Notes: Use will-change: transform on the target element for smoother compositing

results.Framework Notes: Select items with a stable class/data-attribute (not array index) so re-renders in React don't break targeting; Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
results.Do: Keep per-item stagger delay small (0.02-0.04s) for lists longer than 10 items
results.Don't: Don't stagger by more than 0.1s per item on long lists; total reveal time becomes sluggish
results.Performance Notes: For virtualized lists, only animate items currently mounted in the DOM

results.GSAP Snippet: const split = new SplitText(headline, { type: 'chars' }); gsap.from(split.chars, { opacity: 0, y: 20, rotateX: -40, duration: 0.6, stagger: 0.015, ease: 'expo.out' });
results.Framework Notes: SplitText is included with GSAP 3.13+; register it before use, review the current GSAP license, and keep a plain-text fade fallback; Use gsap.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip character motion and render the readable final state immediately
results.Do: Revert SplitText on unmount/cleanup (split.revert()) to restore original text nodes for accessibility tools
results.Don't: Don't split-animate long paragraphs; reserve for short headlines (under ~8 words)
results.Performance Notes: Splitting text creates one element per character; keep it to headline-length copy only for DOM size

results.GSAP Snippet: gsap.from('.grid-item', { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92, y: 16, duration: 0.4, stagger: { each: 0.06, from: 'start', grid: 'auto' }, ease: 'back.out(1.4)' });
results.Framework Notes: grid: 'auto' lets GSAP infer rows/columns from a CSS grid layout for a natural wave stagger; Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
results.Do: Combine with from: 'center' for a bento-grid layout to draw the eye inward first
results.Don't: Don't use back.out on dense data tables; the overshoot reads as sloppy on informational UI
results.Performance Notes: Group DOM writes; avoid interleaving layout reads (getBoundingClientRect) between staggered tweens

results.GSAP Snippet: const reduced = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'); let timer; let onscreen = true; const stop = () => { clearInterval(timer); timer = undefined; }; const start = () => { stop(); if (!reduced.matches && !document.hidden && onscreen) timer = setInterval(nextSlide, 5000); }; const sync = () => reduced.matches ? (stop(), showSlide(activeIndex)) : start(); const observer = new IntersectionObserver(([entry]) => { onscreen = entry.isIntersecting; onscreen ? sync() : stop(); }); const onVisibility = () => document.hidden ? stop() : sync(); observer.observe(root); root.addEventListener('focusin', stop); root.addEventListener('pointerenter', stop); document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', onVisibility); reduced.addEventListener('change', sync); sync(); return () => { stop(); observer.disconnect(); root.removeEventListener('focusin', stop); root.removeEventListener('pointerenter', stop); document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', onVisibility); reduced.removeEventListener('change', sync); };
results.Framework Notes: Use one cancellable timer; pause on focus, hover, offscreen, or hidden visibility; remove every listener and clear the timer on unmount; reduced motion stops rotation and renders the active slide as the final state
results.Do: Provide previous/next and play/pause controls; announce the current slide without moving focus
results.Don't: Don't auto-advance without a visible stop control or continue while focus is inside
results.Performance Notes: IntersectionObserver stops animation offscreen; visibilitychange stops hidden-tab work; cleanup disconnects the observer and clears the timer and listeners

results.GSAP Snippet: const tween = gsap.to('.skeleton', { backgroundPosition: '200% 0', duration: 1.4, ease: 'sine.inOut', repeat: -1 }); return () => tween.kill();
results.Framework Notes: Kill the tween when content mounts or the component unmounts; pause it when its IntersectionObserver reports offscreen or document.visibilityState is hidden; when '(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)' matches kill the tween and set the final static skeleton state
results.Do: Use a CSS gradient background-position sweep rather than opacity pulsing; reads as 'loading' more clearly
results.Don't: Don't run more than one shimmer loop per skeleton group; sync them under one timeline so the wave reads as a single unit
results.Performance Notes: repeat: -1 tweens are cheap but must be explicitly killed on unmount or they leak in SPA route changes

results.GSAP Snippet: gsap.from(el, { opacity: 0, y: 12, duration: 0.35, ease: 'power1.out', scrollTrigger: { trigger: el, start: 'top 90%', toggleActions: 'play none none reverse' } });
results.Framework Notes: Requires the ScrollTrigger plugin registered once via gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger); Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
results.Do: Keep the y offset small (8-16px) so it reads as a fade, not a slide
results.Don't: Don't reveal below-the-fold content needed for SEO/crawlers as invisible-by-default without a no-JS fallback
results.Performance Notes: toggleActions 'play none none reverse' avoids re-triggering on every scroll direction change

results.GSAP Snippet: gsap.to('.bg-layer', { yPercent: 10, ease: 'none', scrollTrigger: { trigger: section, scrub: true } });
results.Framework Notes: Apply parallax to background/decorative layers only, never to text or interactive controls; Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
results.Do: Keep the yPercent delta small (5-15) so foreground and background never desync distractingly
results.Don't: Don't parallax body copy; it hurts reading comfort and can trigger motion sickness
results.Performance Notes: will-change: transform on the parallax layer only; remove it after scroll settles to free GPU memory

results.When to Use: Data has a time axis; user needs to observe rise/fall trends or rate of change over a continuous period
results.When NOT to Use: Fewer than 4 data points (use stat card); more than 6 series (visual noise); no time dimension exists
results.Data Volume Threshold: <1000 pts: SVG; ≥1000 pts: Canvas + downsampling; >10000: aggregate to intervals
results.Color Guidance: Primary: #0080FF. Multiple series: distinct colors + distinct line styles. Fill: 20% opacity
results.Accessibility Notes: Use solid, dashed, and dotted line styles plus direct series labels; never distinguish series by hue alone.
results.A11y Fallback: Visible data table plus concise trend summary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores the full range.

results.Keywords: anomaly, outlier, spike, alert, detection, monitoring, deviation, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
results.When to Use: Monitoring a time-series for outliers; alerting users to unexpected spikes or dips in operational data
results.When NOT to Use: Anomalies are predefined categories (use bar with highlight); real-time context without a pause control
results.Data Volume Threshold: Stream at ≤60fps with Canvas; batch: up to 10,000 pts; mark anomalies as a separate data layer
results.Color Guidance: Normal: #0080FF solid line. Anomaly marker: #FF0000 circle + filled. Alert band: #FFF3CD background zone
results.Accessibility Notes: Mark anomalies with a distinct shape and text annotation as well as color. Do not rely on color alone.
results.A11y Fallback: Anomaly event list/table plus narrative alert summary. Keyboard: focus reveals point details; alerts are available in the persistent list without hover.

results.Accessibility Notes: Use solid actual and dashed forecast lines, direct labels, and a named confidence range; hue alone is insufficient.
results.A11y Fallback: Visible forecast table plus uncertainty summary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; buttons toggle actual/forecast; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores range.

results.Don't: Serve legacy global scripts or import addons from deprecated examples/js paths
results.Code Good: npm install three@0.185.1; import * as THREE from 'three'; import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js'; import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';
results.Code Bad: <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js"></script> // legacy global build with no module graph

results.Description: Load GSAP from its own CDN script tag before your scene script. In bundler projects install via npm and import. GSAP is a completely separate library from Three.js — never try to import it from the Three.js package.
results.Do: Load GSAP CDN before the scene script; or npm install gsap and import separately
results.Don't: Import gsap from three or expect it to be defined without a separate load
results.Code Good: <!-- CDN: load GSAP before your scene script --> <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/gsap/3.12.2/gsap.min.js"></script> <!-- Bundler: --> // import gsap from 'gsap'; import { ScrollTrigger } from 'gsap/ScrollTrigger';
results.Code Bad: import gsap from 'three'; // undefined — GSAP has nothing to do with Three.js

results.Description: Call raycaster.setFromCamera(mouse camera) and then raycaster.intersectObjects(targets true) inside the animate() loop. setFromCamera must come before intersectObjects every frame — without it the raycaster uses a stale ray direction.
results.Do: Call setFromCamera then intersectObjects in order inside every animate() frame
results.Don't: Call intersectObjects without calling setFromCamera first — the raycaster uses a stale or zero ray
results.Code Good: function animate() { requestAnimationFrame(animate); raycaster.setFromCamera(mouse, camera); // update ray direction first const hits = raycaster.intersectObjects(targets, true); // then test intersections if (hits.length > 0) { document.body.style.cursor = 'pointer'; } else { document.body.style.cursor = 'auto'; } renderer.render(scene, camera); }
results.Code Bad: function animate() { requestAnimationFrame(animate); const hits = raycaster.intersectObjects(targets, true); // BUG: setFromCamera never called — stale ray — hits is always empty renderer.render(scene, camera); }

results.Description: Create exactly one Raycaster instance outside all event handlers. Store mouse coordinates in pointermove (cheap). Call setFromCamera and intersectObjects together inside the animate() loop — once per frame instead of once per mouse event.
results.Do: Create one Raycaster; store mouse in pointermove; call setFromCamera + intersectObjects inside animate()
results.Don't: Create a new THREE.Raycaster() inside a mousemove handler or call setFromCamera inside the event listener
results.Code Good: const raycaster = new THREE.Raycaster(); const mouse = new THREE.Vector2(); canvas.addEventListener('pointermove', e => { // only store coords — no raycasting here mouse.x = (e.clientX / canvas.clientWidth) * 2 - 1; mouse.y = -(e.clientY / canvas.clientHeight) * 2 + 1; }); // setFromCamera and intersectObjects run once per frame in animate()
results.Code Bad: window.addEventListener('mousemove', e => { const rc = new THREE.Raycaster(); // new allocation per event rc.setFromCamera(mouse, camera); rc.intersectObjects(targets, true); // fires 200+ times/sec });

results.Description: Set document.body.style.cursor = 'pointer' when intersections are found and reset to 'auto' when none are found. Without cursor feedback users cannot discover that 3D objects are interactive.
results.Do: Update cursor to pointer on hit; reset to auto on miss in the same animate loop block
results.Don't: Run raycasting and read hits without ever updating the cursor style
results.Code Bad: raycaster.setFromCamera(mouse, camera); raycaster.intersectObjects(targets, true); // hits ignored — cursor never changes — objects feel non-interactive

results.Description: Use THREE.LOD to automatically swap high-detail and low-detail geometry as objects move closer or farther from the camera. This maintains frame rate in scenes with many objects spread across a large depth range.
results.Do: Use THREE.LOD to reduce triangle count on distant objects automatically
results.Don't: Render the same high-polygon geometry for every object regardless of its distance from the camera
results.Code Good: const lod = new THREE.LOD(); lod.addLevel(highDetailMesh, 0); // used when < 15 units away lod.addLevel(medDetailMesh, 15); // 15–50 units lod.addLevel(lowDetailMesh, 50); // 50+ units scene.add(lod);
results.Code Bad: scene.add(highDetailMesh); // 64k-triangle mesh rendered at full cost whether 1 unit or 100 units from camera

results.Description: Cap devicePixelRatio at 2. Retina displays report 3x or higher. Going from 2x to 3x multiplies pixel count by 2.25x with no visible quality improvement at normal viewing distance.
results.Do: Apply Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, 2) — cap is at 2 not at 3
results.Don't: Pass window.devicePixelRatio directly without any cap
results.Code Bad: renderer.setPixelRatio(window.devicePixelRatio); // 3x display = 9 pixels per CSS pixel = 2.25x GPU cost for zero quality gain

results.Description: Use the minimum segment count that achieves the desired silhouette quality. Hero objects: 32–64 segments. Background objects: 8–16. Particle stand-ins: 6–8. High counts on background geometry waste GPU draw calls with zero visible benefit.
results.Do: Apply a tiered segment budget based on the visual priority of each object in the scene
results.Don't: Default every sphere and cylinder to 64+ segments regardless of its role
results.Code Good: const bgSphere = new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.5, 8, 8); // background const heroSphere = new THREE.SphereGeometry(1, 64, 64); // foreground product
results.Code Bad: const particleSphere = new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.1, 64, 64); // 64 segments × 1000 particles = massive overdraw

results.Description: Add role='img' and a descriptive aria-label to renderer.domElement after appending it to the DOM. Screen readers receive no information from a WebGL canvas — the aria-label is the only description they can announce to users.
results.Do: Set role='img' and a meaningful aria-label on renderer.domElement before or after appending it
results.Don't: Append the canvas to the DOM with no accessibility attributes — invisible to screen readers
results.Code Good: renderer.domElement.setAttribute('role', 'img'); renderer.domElement.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Interactive 3D product viewer. Drag to rotate. Scroll to zoom.'); document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement);
results.Code Bad: document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement); // bare canvas — screen readers announce nothing

results.Description: Check window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') before starting any auto-rotation, particle animation, or camera movement. Users who enable this OS preference have motion sickness or vestibular disorders. IMPORTANT: reading .matches once at page load is a one-time snapshot — if the user changes their OS accessibility setting mid-session the scene will not react. Attach a 'change' listener to the MediaQueryList so noMotion stays in sync at runtime.
results.Do: Use matchMedia.addEventListener('change') to keep noMotion reactive; gate all auto-animation on the live value
results.Don't: Read .matches once at startup and never update it — the scene ignores mid-session OS setting changes
results.Code Good: const mq = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'); let noMotion = mq.matches; mq.addEventListener('change', e => { noMotion = e.matches; }); // In animate(): if (!noMotion) { mesh.rotation.y += dt * 0.8; particles.rotation.y += dt * 0.1; }
results.Code Bad: const noMotion = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches; // one-time snapshot — mid-session OS change is ignored entirely

results.Guideline: Tone Mapping and Output Color Space
results.Description: Three.js color management is enabled by default. Keep working colors in the linear-sRGB space and set the renderer output color space to SRGBColorSpace; choose tone mapping when rendering HDR lighting to a display.
results.Do: Use the default ColorManagement.enabled state and set renderer.outputColorSpace plus an appropriate toneMapping
results.Don't: Disable color management or use removed outputEncoding and sRGBEncoding properties
results.Code Good: THREE.ColorManagement.enabled = true; renderer.outputColorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace; renderer.toneMapping = THREE.ACESFilmicToneMapping; renderer.toneMappingExposure = 1.0;

results.Description: Use GSAP timelines for any animation with more than two sequential steps or for scroll-linked camera paths. GSAP timelines can be paused reversed and scrubbed — far more maintainable than boolean state machines.
results.Do: Use GSAP timelines for sequences with more than two steps and for scroll-driven animations
results.Don't: Implement multi-step sequences with boolean flags and manual frame counters
results.Code Good: const tl = gsap.timeline({ defaults: { ease: 'power2.out' } }); tl.from(mesh.position, { y: -3, duration: 1 }) .to(mesh.rotation, { y: Math.PI, duration: 1 }, '-=0.3') .to(camera.position, { z: 2, duration: 1.5 });
results.Code Bad: let step = 0; let t = 0; function animate() { if (step === 0 && (t += 0.01) >= 1) step = 1; } // grows unmanageable with 3+ steps

results.Description: The antialias option can only be set at WebGLRenderer construction time. Setting renderer.antialias after construction has absolutely no effect — the WebGL context is already created without it. Decide before instantiating.
results.Do: Set antialias:true inside the WebGLRenderer constructor options object
results.Don't: Construct the renderer without antialias then try to enable it by assigning the property
results.Code Good: const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true, alpha: true }); // antialias baked into the WebGL context
results.Code Bad: const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer(); renderer.antialias = true; // no effect — context created without AA — edges remain aliased

results.Description: CapsuleGeometry is part of the current Three.js geometry API and directly creates a capsule from radius length cap segments and radial segments.
results.Do: Construct current capsule meshes with THREE.CapsuleGeometry
results.Don't: Rebuild a standard capsule from separate cylinder and sphere meshes unless custom topology is required
results.Code Good: const geometry = new THREE.CapsuleGeometry(0.5, 1, 4, 8); const capsule = new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material);
results.Code Bad: const body = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.5, 0.5, 1); // unnecessary multi-mesh workaround

pattern.name: Scroll-Triggered Storytelling
pattern.sections: Intro hook > Chapter 1 (problem) > Chapter 2 (journey) > Chapter 3 (solution) > Climax CTA
pattern.cta_placement: End of each chapter (mini) + Final climax CTA
pattern.color_strategy: Progressive reveal. Each chapter has distinct color. Building intensity.
pattern.conversion: Keep the narrative understandable without scroll-driven effects. Use progress indicator. Mobile: simplify animations. Keep DOM reading order complete; disable parallax and scroll-scrub under reduced motion.
